subject: Architecture
title: New Orleans: Below Sea Level by Design
description: A micro-lesson that makes New Orleans: Below Sea Level by Design usable.

hook.text: Half of New Orleans sits below sea level — protected only by levees. Hurricane Katrina showed the cost of that bet.

buildup.text: French colonists built the city on a Mississippi River delta — swampy, flood-prone, and sinking naturally.

discovery.text: Draining swamps for development dried and compressed the soil — causing the city to sink below the river.

twist.text: In 2005, Hurricane Katrina breached the levees. 80% of the city flooded, killing over 1,800 people.

climax.text: A $14.5 billion flood protection system was built — the largest civil works project in U.S. history.

punchline.text: Building below sea level works fine. Until the walls fail.

quiz.question: Why did New Orleans sink below sea level?
options: Rising sea levels gradually covered the coastal lowlands
Draining swamps for development compressed the soil
Mining operations removed ground material beneath the city

details.summary: Much of New Orleans sits below sea level, protected by a system of levees that catastrophically failed during Hurricane Katrina in 2005. The city's pumping system, which drains rainwater out of the bowl-shaped terrain, creates a paradox: the more it pumps, the more the land sinks.
details.whyItMatters: New Orleans proves that engineering cannot indefinitely defy geography. Levees, pumps, and drainage create a false sense of security that collapses when the system's weakest link fails, as Katrina devastatingly demonstrated.
takeaways: Much of New Orleans sits below sea level behind levees
Hurricane Katrina exposed catastrophic failures in 2005
Pumping rainwater out causes further land subsidence

faq.question: How much of New Orleans is below sea level?
faq.answer: Roughly 50% of the city sits below sea level, with some neighborhoods as much as 3 meters (10 feet) below. The entire city relies on levees, floodwalls, and constant pumping to stay dry. Before Katrina, these systems had not been tested by a major hurricane in decades.

faq.question: What failed during Hurricane Katrina?
faq.answer: The Army Corps of Engineers' levee system failed at over 50 points, flooding 80% of the city. Investigations found design flaws, poor construction quality, and inadequate soil analysis. The failures were engineering errors, not acts of nature — the storm itself was within expected parameters.
